fact_text: The analyst frames buying a share as becoming an equal partner with top-quality Pakistani businessmen, not average ones, so financial statements are read to judge the business's compounding ability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Statements must also be checked for whether minority shareholders are true equal partners, because a good business still fails to create wealth if majority owners extract more profit than outsiders receive.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats future return on invested capital as the best ratio for finding top businesses: how much profit a given investment will earn going forward.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Long-term share price growth per year tends to follow the business's future ROIC, so a business with future ROIC of 30% could grow wealth about 15 times over 10 years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Estimating future ROIC needs two inputs from the statements: the business's future profits and the investment required to earn those profits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Before reading numbers, one must know what the business does: its main product or service, how it is priced and its main raw materials; numbers have no value without that understanding.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Product pricing and further revenue information come from the revenue section of the accounts, while the important raw materials are visible in the cost of sales notes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Reading a cement maker's cost of sales shows coal and electricity as the two main raw material costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Following statements over time shows whether a business's inflows and outflows are dollar-linked, government-priced or set by international prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Quarterly statements should be read as owners reporting to you every three months, with the aim of understanding the business like an owner.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Financial numbers are a result of the business, and past numbers do not determine future numbers; understanding the business lets one project the next quarters' statements.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Even Warren Buffett cannot decide from numbers alone without knowing the business; accounting is only a starting point and there is no shortcut of reading just the figures.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For each industry, identify the business's main problem and know where in the statements that information sits; the key lines to watch differ by sector.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: External dynamics affect financial statements with a lag of about three to six months.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For power companies, profit is not the issue; the real problem is circular debt and cash flow, so compare profit after tax against the rise in trade debts over the same period.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For oil and gas exploration companies, the main problem is circular debt and cash flow, so check whether profit after tax was absorbed by a rise in trade debts.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Autos have no cash flow problem because vehicles are sold in advance and payment arrives first; the key is that the car is a number-one product with an upward sales trend, visible in the revenue section.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Profit per car, tractor or bike can be checked by dividing net profit by units sold, alongside net margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pharmaceutical plants are not very expensive, so the main drivers are medicine prices and raw material prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Medicine price changes can be seen in the revenue section or from the market, and the cost of sales shows whether imported raw material prices are trending up or down.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Local pharmaceutical companies have a longer cash cycle than multinationals, so for a local one trade debts and stock-in-trade should be tracked to see whether they grow along with revenue.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For refineries the key variable is petrol and diesel prices versus crude oil price, the refinery margin, which can be derived from the revenue and cost of sales sections.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under-invoicing or off-the-book sales of 10% could make reported profit about 50% lower than actual profit, which wrecks the equal-partner position.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Revenue and cost of sales are the two lines to master: the analyst says understanding them covers about 75% of the work, since misrepresentation there often shows nowhere else in the accounts.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Company size does not protect against off-book sales: large sugar companies with hundreds of billions in revenue are said to have substantial off-book sales, while a small firm supplying renowned FMCG buyers cannot do it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says off-the-book sales are quite common in the sugar sector even though revenues run into hundreds of billions of rupees.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Exports are another place where sales may be misreported, with claims of real sales of $5 shown as $100 on the books, especially now that income is taxed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To judge off-book sale risk, study the supply chain, who the buyers are and whether they would tolerate under-invoicing, and also the business's market reputation; any real doubt means avoiding the stock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cost of sales and admin expenses are where over-invoicing risk is higher: an importer may show a $100 input at $5 on paper, or the reverse, to cut reported profit and keep dollars abroad.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Check import over-invoicing by comparing the price paid for a raw material against an international index such as oil, coal or cotton each quarter; a one-quarter spike is suspicious, since firms do not over-invoice 2% every quarter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Salaries can be padded in admin or cost of sales; compare admin expense as a percentage of revenue with competitors in the same industry and raise it at the AGM or corporate briefing if it is high.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Revenue can be pre-booked by showing a sale early, for example shipping product to a friend and having it returned next quarter; the analyst notes such accounting fraud has happened even in the US.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over-invoicing plant and machinery, such as booking $50 million of a $100 million capex while owners keep the rest abroad, lowers ROIC and lets owners enjoy more of the profits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Companies can capitalise regular repairs and maintenance capex, which cuts expenses and lifts reported profit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The auditor is a limited watchdog: a tier-two auditor will most probably approve things like excessive salaries or over-invoicing if documents are supplied.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Private banks are the second watchdog: if a company's loans come mostly from public banks, be alert, since private banks may be uncomfortable lending and the accounts may be weaker.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW TO READ FINANCIAL STATEMENTS LIKE A PRO' (YouTube transcript, undated)
